chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Sammal from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) who said:
"The woman who undergoes khul' (redemption/divorce by mutual consent) is followed by divorce as long as she is in her waiting period."

And those of our companions who went early established the correctness of what we have gone towards by the saying of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If the matter were in our hands, we would validate only the divorce of the Sunnah.'
And Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah and others established by saying: 'It is established that divorce does not occur by condition, and part of the condition of khul' is that the man says:
If you return what you gave, then I will have control over your body,
And Ibn Sama'ah also established by what he narrated:

key_terms.طَلاَقَ اَلسُّنَّةِ: The divorce of the Sunnah (preferred/standard divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of khul' in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes that khul' functions as a revocable divorce during the 'iddah, a ruling supported by early Shia scholars who cite the Imam’s preference for 'talaq al-sunnah' to highlight khul' as a conditional, less ideal dissolution. The debate centers on whether khul' constitutes a binding divorce or a conditional stipulation, with scholars like Ibn Sama'a arguing that since khul' involves a condition ('if you return what you gave'), it may not effect an immediate, irrevocable separation like standard talaq. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the procedural integrity of divorce and the Imam's authority in validating marital dissolutions.
